autonomous-loop, convergence-detection, externalized-state, fresh-context, research-agent, JSONL-state, strategy-file -->\n\n# Autonomous Deep Research Loop\n\nNote: `Task` is allowed for the command executor that manages the loop. The `@deep-research` agent itself is LEAF-only and does not dispatch sub-agents.\n\nIterative research protocol with fresh context per iteration, externalized state, and convergence detection for deep technical investigation.\n\nRuntime path resolution: OpenCode/Copilot runtime uses `.opencode/agents/*.md`; Claude runtime uses `.claude/agents/*.md`.\n\nOperator contract precedence for this skill surface (highest first): command entrypoint syntax in `.opencode/commands/deep/research.md`; convergence math in `references/convergence/convergence.md` and the deep-research YAML workflow; runtime agent inventories from the checked-in runtime directories above.\n\n### Convergence Threshold Semantics\n\n**Default:** 0.05 on newInfoRatio (fully-new=1.0, partially-new=0.5, +0.10 simplicity bonus, capped 1.0)\n\n**Semantic:** `convergenceThreshold` compares newly discovered information against accumulated research knowledge with negative-knowledge emphasis. Lower = more iterations / higher signal threshold.\n\n**NOT INTERCHANGEABLE with siblings:**\n- `deep-review` uses 0.10 default on weighted P0/P1/P2 severity ratio\n- `deep-ai-council` uses 0.20 default on adjudicator-verdict stability\n\nCarrying threshold expectations across siblings will cause unexpected iteration counts; see this skill's changelog/decision records for the parity research confirming thresholds do not carry across siblings.\n\n## 1. WHEN TO USE\n\n### Activation Triggers\n\nUse this skill when:\n- Deep investigation requiring multiple rounds of discovery\n- Topic spans 3+ technical domains or sources\n- Initial findings need progressive refinement\n- Overnight or unattended research sessions\n- Research where prior findings inform subsequent queries\n\nKeyword triggers:\n\n- `autoresearch`\n- `deep research`\n- `autonomous research`\n- `research loop`\n- `iterative research`\n- `multi-round research`\n- `deep investigation`\n- `comprehensive research`\n\n### Use Cases\n\nUse deep-research for multi-round technical investigation, source triangulation, repeated exploration with fresh context, and research sessions where prior findings should shape the next focus.\n\n### When NOT to Use\n\n- Simple, single-question research (use direct codebase search or `/speckit:plan`)\n- Known-solution documentation (use `/speckit:plan`)\n- Implementation tasks (use `/speckit:implement`)\n- Quick codebase searches (use `@context` or direct Grep/Glob)\n- Fewer than 3 sources needed (single-pass research suffices)\n\n---\n\n## 2. SMART ROUTING\n\n> Pattern: aligned with the [sk-doc smart-router resilience template](../../sk-doc/create-skill/assets/skill/skill-smart-router.md).\n\n### Resource Domains\n\nThe router discovers markdown resources from `references/` and `assets/`, then applies intent scoring from `RESOURCE_MAP`. Keep routing domain-focused rather than hardcoding exhaustive inventories.\n\n- `references/guides/quick-reference.md` -- first-touch operator cheat sheet.\n- `references/protocol/loop-protocol.md` -- lifecycle, dispatch, reducer sequencing, command-owned state flow.\n- `references/protocol/spec-check-protocol.md` -- bounded `spec.md` anchoring and generated-fence write-back.\n- `references/convergence*.md` -- stop contracts, signals, recovery, graph gates, reference-only convergence ideas.\n- `references/state*.md` -- packet layout, JSONL records, markdown outputs, reducer ownership, reconstruction.\n- `references/guides/capability-matrix.md` -- runtime parity.\n- `assets/*.md` -- markdown templates and prompt assets safe for guarded markdown loading.\n\n### Resource Loading Levels\n\n| Level | When to Load | Resources |\n|-------|--------------|-----------|\n| ALWAYS | Every skill invocation | Quick reference baseline |\n| CONDITIONAL | If intent signals match | Loop, convergence, state, spec anchoring, runtime parity references |\n| ON_DEMAND | Only on explicit request | Full reference set and markdown assets |\n\n### Phase Signals\n\n| Phase | Signal | Primary Resources |\n|-------|--------|-------------------|\n| Init | No JSONL exists or setup context | `loop-protocol.md`, `state-format.md`, `state-jsonl.md` |\n| Iteration | Dispatch context includes iteration number | `loop-protocol.md`, `state-outputs.md`, `convergence-signals.md` |\n| Stuck | Dispatch context includes recovery language | `convergence-recovery.md`, `state-reducer-registry.md` |\n| Synthesis | STOP candidate or final report | `convergence.md`, `state-outputs.md`, `spec-check-protocol.md` |\n\n### Smart Router Pseudocode\n\nThe authoritative routing logic for scoped loading, weighted intent scoring, ambiguity handling, and graceful fallback, via four patterns: runtime discovery (`discover_markdown_resources()` scans `references/`/`assets/`), existence-check-before-load (`load_if_available()` guards paths against `inventory` and `seen`), extensible routing keys (intent labels map to resource families, not static _task_text(task) -> str:\n    return \" \".join([\n        str(getattr(task, \"text\", \"\")),\n        str(getattr(task, \"query\", \"\")),\n        \" \".join(getattr(task, \"keywords\", []) or {\"intents\": intents, \"intent_scores\": scores, \"resources\": loaded}\n    if not matched_intents:\n        result[\"notice\"] = f\"No knowledge base found for intent(s): {', '.join(intents)}\"\n    return result\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. HOW IT WORKS\n\n### Invocation Contract\n\nThis skill is invoked exclusively through `/deep:research:auto` or `/deep:research:confirm` -- the command YAML owns state, dispatch, convergence, and synthesis. Never simulate the loop with ad hoc shell dispatch, nested CLI loops, direct `@deep-research` Task dispatch, `/tmp` prompt files, or state outside the resolved local research packet.\n\n### Executor Selection Contract\n\nThe YAML workflow owns executor selection (native `@deep-research` by default, or a routed CLI executor -- never ad hoc shell loops). Cross-CLI delegation inside an executor sandbox is possible but discouraged: do not invoke the same CLI from within itself, and do not assume auth propagates to child CLIs. Per-kind dispatch branches (`native`, `cli-opencode`, `cli-claude-code`) and flag-compatibility rules are in [loop-protocol.md §3](references/protocol/loop-protocol.md).\n\nExecutor invariants:\n\n1. Produce a non-empty iteration markdown file at `{state_paths.iteration_pattern}`.\n2. Append a JSONL delta record to `{state_paths.state_log}` with required fields: `type`, `iteration`, `newInfoRatio`, `status`, and `focus`.\n3. Respect the LEAF-agent constraint: no sub-dispatch, no nested loops, and max 12 tool calls per iteration.\n\nFailure modes include `iteration_file_missing`, `iteration_file_empty`, `jsonl_not_appended`, `jsonl_missing_fields`, and `jsonl_parse_error`. Three consecutive failures route to stuck recovery.\n\n### Lifecycle Contract\n\nRuntime-supported lifecycle modes:\n\n| Mode | Meaning |\n|------|---------|\n| `new` | First run against the spec folder |\n| `resume` | Continue the active lineage and append a typed `resumed` JSONL event |\n| `restart` | Archive the existing research tree, mint a fresh `sessionId`, increment `generation`, and append a typed `restarted` event |\n\nDeferred modes `fork` and `completed-continue` are reserved but not runtime-supported.\n\n### Code-Graph Readiness TrustState Surface\n\nThe live code-graph readiness contract reaches four TrustState values: `live`, `stale`, `absent`, and `unavailable`. `cached`, `imported`, `rebuilt`, and `rehomed` remain declared in the shared TrustState type for compatibility, but the readiness helpers used here do not emit them today.\n\n### Resource Map Integration\n\nWhen `{spec_folder}/resource-map.md` exists at init, `resource_map_present: true` is persisted, the map is summarized into `deep-research-strategy.md` `Known Context`, and listed files count as known inventory (gaps flagged only when missing from the map). When absent, `resource_map_present: false` is persisted and the loop continues normally -- absence is informational, not a failure. Full field-level rules live in [state-outputs.md §6](references/state/state-outputs.md).\n\n### Bounded Context Snapshot Replacement\n\nFor codebase-scoped targets, initialization captures a bounded, pointer-based snapshot (source paths/symbols, integration points, conventions, and gaps) into `deep-research-strategy.md` `Known Context` -- oriented toward the first iteration, not a substitute for `@context` or `/speckit:plan`. A quiet flag has to decide two things: what the one line looks like, and what happens when a caller asks for both machine formats at once.\n\n**Decision**: `--quiet` prints the same label the report prints, on its own line, with no leading blank line. A `--quiet` and `--json` invocation is a usage error: the message goes to stderr, stdout stays empty, and the exit code is 1.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- A caller can move from `grep '^Recommended Level:'` on the report to `--quiet` without changing its pattern.\n- The label becomes a public contract, so a future rename is a breaking change that needs its own packet.\n- A contradictory invocation fails loudly instead of producing output the caller did not ask for, at the cost of one more error message to document.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Bare integer output (`0`): it is marginally easier to consume but drops the level name and gives a caller no stable prefix to anchor on.\n- `--quiet` wins over `--json`: silent precedence produces a text line for a caller that asked for JSON, which is the failure mode hardest to notice.\n- A new `--format level` option: a larger surface for the same one-line result, and it would invite a second format later.\n\n---\n\n","_meta":{"cognition.ai/linesAdded":87,"cognition.ai/linesRemoved":88}}],"rawInput":{"file_path":"/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.worktrees/223-deepseek-final/specs/zz-bench-authoring/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag/plan.md"},"_meta":{"cognition.ai/inferenceToolName":"write"}}

This packet adds a --quiet flag that prints exactly that one line and leaves every other output path unchanged.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"recommend level quiet flag\"\n  - \"add a quiet flag to recommend level sh\"\nimportance_tier: \"normal\"\ncontextType: \"general\"\n---\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core + level2-verify + level3-arch | v2.3 -->\n# Feature Specification: Add a quiet flag to recommend-level.sh\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->\n\n\n---\n\n## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY\n\n`recommend-level.sh` answers one question — which documentation level a task earns — but it answers it inside a sixteen-line human report for its simplest input and seventeen lines for a scored feature. A caller that wants only the number has to grep a label out of that report and assume the line it wants stays where it is.\n\nThis packet adds a `--quiet` flag that prints exactly one line, `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`, and changes nothing else. Every invocation without the flag keeps its current bytes, and every invocation with `--json` keeps its current JSON document.\n\n**Key Decisions**: reuse the label `output_text()` already prints instead of inventing a second format, and reject `--quiet` combined with `--json` as a usage error rather than letting one silently win.\n\n**Critical Dependencies**: the argument parser and the `output_text()` emitter inside `recommend-level.sh`. No new package, and no other script reads this output.\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## 1. METADATA\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| **Level** | 3 |\n| **Priority** | P1 |\n| **Status** | Draft |\n| **Created** | 2026-10-25 |\n| **Branch** | `worktrees/223-deepseek-final` |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->\n## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE\n\n### Problem Statement\n\nThe script's text output is built for a human reader: a blank line, the level line, a score line, a blank line, a six-row breakdown, a blank line, and a four-line phase block. A build script, a hook, or a person in a pipeline that needs only the level must pipe that report through `grep`, `sed`, or `awk`, and each of those callers hard-codes an assumption about which line carries the answer. When the report grows, as it did when the phase block was added, the assumption is still true by luck rather than by contract.\n\n### Purpose\n\nOne invocation, one line, one value: a caller reads the recommended level without parsing a report.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n- Add a `--quiet` option to the argument parser in `recommend-level.sh`.\n- Print exactly the recommended-level line when `--quiet` is present, with no leading blank line and no trailing report sections.\n- Reject `--quiet` combined with `--json` as a usage error on stderr with exit code 1.\n- Document the flag in the `show_help()` usage text and in the script's header OPTIONS block.\n- Prove the default output is byte-identical to the pre-change baseline.\n\n### Out of Scope\n- Changing any scoring weight, threshold, or level mapping - the flag changes output only, and touching the algorithm would make the regression proof meaningless.\n- Adding a `-q` short alias - the request names `--quiet`, and a second spelling doubles the option surface for no caller.\n- Updating the documents that invoke the script without flags (`references/workflows/spec-authoring-card.md`, `references/workflows/quick-reference.md`) - they never pass `--quiet`, so their commands stay correct.\n- Refactoring `output_text()` into smaller helpers - a pure refactor would add review surface to a change whose proof is \"the bytes did not move\".\n\n### Files to Change\n\n| File Path | Change Type | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Modify | Add the `--quiet` case, the `QUIET` global, the conflict check, the one-line emitter, and the two documentation blocks |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-001 | `--quiet` is accepted at any position in the argument list and consumes no value. |\n| REQ-002 | With `--quiet`, stdout holds exactly one line, `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`, terminated by a newline, with no leading blank line. |\n| REQ-003 | Without `--quiet`, stdout is byte-identical to the pre-change output for every input, including the leading blank line and the phase block. |\n| REQ-004 | `--quiet` combined with `--json` writes a conflict message to stderr, writes nothing to stdout, and exits 1. |\n| REQ-005 | `--quiet` preserves the existing exit codes: 0 for a successful recommendation, 1 for invalid input. |\n\n### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-006 | `show_help()` lists `--quiet` and states that it prints only the recommended-level line. |\n| REQ-007 | The script header OPTIONS block documents `--quiet` beside the existing flags. |\n| REQ-008 | `--quiet` composes with `--no-recommend-phases` and `--phase-threshold` without changing the one-line output. |\n| REQ-009 | The level line printed under `--quiet` matches the level line the same invocation prints without the flag: same number, same name. |\n| REQ-010 | `--quiet` suppresses stdout report lines only; every existing stderr diagnostic still prints unchanged. |\n\n> Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,\n> which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- **SC-001**: **Given** the current script, **When** `bash recommend-level.sh --loc 50 --files 2` runs, **Then** stdout is 16 lines and its second line is `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)`.\n- **SC-002**: **Given** the flag is implemented, **When** `bash recommend-level.sh --quiet --loc 50 --files 2` runs, **Then** stdout is exactly one line and `wc -l` prints 1.\n- **SC-003**: **Given** the flag is implemented, **When** `bash recommend-level.sh --quiet --loc 500 --files 15 --auth --api --db --architectural` runs, **Then** stdout is `Recommended Level: 3 (Full)` and exit status is 0.\n- **SC-004**: **Given** the captured baseline of the default output, **When** `diff scratch/baseline-default.txt <(bash recommend-level.sh --loc 50 --files 2)` runs, **Then** it prints nothing and exits 0.\n- **SC-005**: **Given** `--quiet` and `--json` are both present, **When** the script runs, **Then** stderr names the conflict, stdout is empty, and exit status is 1.\n- **SC-006**: **Given** `--quiet` is absent, **When** the two Node phase suites run, **Then** both exit 0 and their `--json` fixtures parse unchanged.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:risks -->\n## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |\n|------|------|--------|------------|\n| Dependency | Bash 3.2 or newer on macOS | The script already requires it; `set -euo pipefail` and `[[ ]]` are used throughout | No new requirement; the flag adds no construct the script does not already use |\n| Risk | A future edit renames the `Recommended Level:` label and breaks callers that now depend on it | Medium | Pin the exact label in an acceptance criterion and a line-level check |\n| Risk | `--quiet` accidentally suppresses stderr, hiding a real input error | High | REQ-010 plus an edge-case check that an invalid `--loc` still prints its error |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->\n\n---\n\n\n## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n- **NFR-P01**: The flag adds no measurable runtime cost; a quiet run stays within the script's current sub-second wall time because it skips work rather than adding it.\n\n### Security\n- **NFR-S01**: N/A - the script reads no credential, writes no file, and makes no network call; the flag changes only which `printf` runs.\n\n### Reliability\n- **NFR-R01**: Exit codes are unchanged for every input class, so a caller that branches on the status keeps its behavior.\n\n---\n\n## 8. EDGE CASES\n\n### Data Boundaries\n- Empty input: `bash recommend-level.sh` with no arguments still prints `ERROR: At least --loc or --files must be provided` to stderr and exits 1, with or without `--quiet`.\n- Maximum length: `--loc 2000 --files 40` still prints one line under `--quiet`; the extreme-scale phase bonus is computed but never rendered.\n\n### Error Scenarios\n- External service failure: N/A - the script calls no service.\n- Network timeout: N/A - the script makes no network call.\n- Invalid argument value: `--loc abc` still exits 1 with `ERROR: --loc must be a positive integer`, and `--quiet` does not swallow it.\n\n### State Transitions\n- Partial completion: `--quiet` passed twice is idempotent; the second occurrence sets the same flag and the output stays one line.\n- Conflicting output modes: `--quiet --json` in either order reaches the same conflict check and exits 1.\n\n---\n\n## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT\n\n| Dimension | Score | Triggers |\n|-----------|-------|----------|\n| Scope | 4/25 | Files: 1, LOC: ~20, Systems: 1 |\n| Risk | 2/25 | Auth: N, API: N, Breaking: N |\n| Research | 2/20 | One read of the parser and the emitter |\n| Multi-Agent | 0/15 | Workstreams: 1 |\n| Coordination | 1/15 | Dependencies: 0 |\n| **Total** | **9/100** | **Level 3** |\n\nThe score reads 9/100 because the change is one branch in one script. Level 3 was assigned by the directive that created this packet, not derived from this score; the score is recorded as measured rather than inflated to match the level.\n\n---\n\n## 10. RISK MATRIX\n\n| Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|\n| R-001 | The default report drifts while the flag is added | H | L | Capture the pre-change output, then diff it after the change |\n| R-002 | A JSON consumer receives a text line because `--quiet` silently outranks `--json` | M | M | Reject the combination with exit 1 instead of picking a winner |\n| R-003 | A caller parses a second line and breaks when the label moves | M | L | Keep the existing label and assert it in an acceptance criterion |\n| R-004 | `--quiet` hides an input error a caller needs to see | H | L | Leave stderr untouched and test the invalid-input path |\n\n---\n\n## 11. USER STORIES\n\n### US-001: One line for a pipeline (Priority: P0)\n\n**As a** build or hook script, **I want** `--quiet` to print only the recommended level, **so that** I can read the value without parsing a human report.\n\n**Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).\n\n---\n\n### US-002: Unchanged report for a person (Priority: P1)\n\n**As a** maintainer running the script by hand, **I want** the default output to stay exactly as it is, **so that** the report I read today does not change under me.\n\n**Acceptance criteria:** see `acceptance-criteria.md` (rows referencing this story).\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:questions -->\n## 12. A quiet mode that echoes the same string a second time would create two producers of a contract that callers parse. A quiet mode that filters the text report instead, by suppressing echoes, would couple the flag to the layout of the report and break whenever a line is added.\n\n**Decision**: Extract `output_level_line()`, have `output_text()` call it in place of its inline echo, and have `output_quiet()` call the same function. `--quiet` becomes a third output mode selected in the dispatch, not a filter applied to the first one.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- The label has one producer, so the quiet line and the report line cannot drift.\n- The text report gains one function call and prints the same bytes, which the baseline diff proves.\n- One more function to name and place; it sits in section 4 beside the other output functions.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Filter the text report with `grep` or `sed` inside the script: the filter would encode the report's layout, and the phase block already makes that layout conditional.\n- Duplicate the echo in a new function: two producers of a parsed contract, and the duplication is exactly the risk R-001 names.\n\n---\n\n### ADR-002: `--quiet` with `--json` is a usage error\n\n**Status**: Proposed\n\n**Context**: The script already has two machine-readable modes. `--quiet` and `--json` each claim stdout, and a caller that passes both has made a mistake that a precedence rule would hide.\n\n**Decision**: After the parse loop, reject the combination with exit 1, a stderr message naming both flags, and an empty stdout. Check it after the loop rather than inside it, so the answer does not depend on flag order.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- A caller cannot silently receive the wrong shape, and the failure is immediate and legible.\n- The existing `--json` callers are unaffected, because neither passes `--quiet`.\n- The guard is one more branch, and it must sit ahead of the quiet branch in the dispatch.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Last flag wins: order-dependent behavior that is invisible in the command line a caller writes.\n- Quiet wins over JSON: a caller that asked for an object would get a string, and its parser would fail somewhere else with no clue why.\n- JSON wins over quiet: the flag would appear to be accepted while doing nothing, which is worse than an error.\n\n---\n","_meta":{"cognition.ai/linesAdded":118,"cognition.ai/linesRemoved":93}}],"rawInput":{"file_path":"/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.worktrees/223-deepseek-final/specs/zz-bench-authoring/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag/plan.md"},"_meta":{"cognition.ai/inferenceToolName":"write"}}

ARCHITECTURE\n\n### Pattern\n\nSingle script, three output modes.\n\n### Key Components\n- **Argument parser (section 5)**: owns flag acceptance, sets `QUIET`, and is the only place a new flag is admitted.\n- **`output_level_line()`**: new. The one producer of the `Recommended Level:` literal, called by both the text report and the quiet path.\n- **`output_quiet()`**: new. Calls `output_level_line()` and returns, so it inherits the label rather than restating it.\n- **`output_text()` / `output_json()`**: behavior unchanged. The text report swaps its inline echo for the shared call and prints the same bytes.\n- **Conflict guard (section 7)**: rejects `--quiet` with `--json` after the parse loop, so flag order cannot change the answer.\n\n### Data Flow\n\nArguments enter the `while`/`case` loop, which sets `QUIET` and the existing flags. `show_help` exits from inside the loop, so `--help` short-circuits every mode. After the loop, validation rejects a non-numeric or empty input. Scoring runs unchanged, `determine_level` sets `RECOMMENDED_LEVEL` and `LEVEL_NAME`, and the dispatch selects one mode in this order: conflict guard, quiet, JSON, text.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:affected-surfaces -->\n## FIX ADDENDUM: AFFECTED SURFACES\n\nThis packet is not a bug fix, but it changes a public output surface that other files consume, so the inventory below is filled rather than skipped.\n\n| Surface | Current Role | Action | Verification |\n|---------|--------------|--------|--------------|\n| `runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Owns argument parsing and all three output modes; Check it after the loop rather than inside it, so the answer does not depend on flag order.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- A caller cannot silently receive the wrong shape, and the failure is immediate and legible.\n- The existing `--json` callers are unaffected, because neither passes `--quiet`.\n- The guard is one more branch, and it must sit ahead of the quiet branch in the dispatch.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Last flag wins: order-dependent behavior that is invisible in the command line a caller writes.\n- Quiet wins over JSON: a caller that asked for an object would get a string, and its parser would fail somewhere else with no clue why.\n- JSON wins over quiet: the flag would appear to be accepted while doing nothing, which is worse than an error.\n\n---\n","newText":"---\ntitle: \"Implementation Plan: Add a quiet flag to recommend-level.sh\"\ndescription: \"Add a third output mode to recommend-level.sh that prints only the recommended-level line, emit that line from one shared function so the literal has a single producer, and prove the three existing shapes are byte-identical.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"recommend level quiet flag plan\"\nimportance_tier: \"normal\"\ncontextType: \"general\"\n---\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: plan-core | v2.3 -->\n# Implementation Plan: Add a quiet flag to recommend-level.sh\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:summary -->\n## 1. A quiet mode that filters the text report instead, by suppressing echoes, would couple the flag to the layout of the report and break whenever a line is added.\n\n**Decision**: Extract `output_level_line()`, have `output_text()` call it in place of its inline echo, and have `output_quiet()` call the same function. `--quiet` becomes a third output mode selected in the dispatch, not a filter applied to the first one.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- The label has one producer, so the quiet line and the report line cannot drift.\n- The text report gains one function call and prints the same bytes, which the baseline diff proves.\n- One more function to name and place; it sits in section 4 beside the other output functions.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Filter the text report with `grep` or `sed` inside the script: the filter would encode the report's layout, and the phase block already makes that layout conditional.\n- Duplicate the echo in a new function: two producers of a parsed contract, and the duplication is exactly the risk R-001 names.\n\n---\n\n### ADR-002: `--quiet` with `--json` is a usage error\n\n**Status**: Proposed\n\n**Context**: The script already has two machine-readable modes. `--quiet` and `--json` each claim stdout, and a caller that passes both has made a mistake that a precedence rule would hide.\n\n**Decision**: After the parse loop, reject the combination with exit 1, a stderr message naming both flags, and an empty stdout. Check it after the loop rather than inside it, so the answer does not depend on flag order.\n\n**Consequences**:\n- A caller cannot silently receive the wrong shape, and the failure is immediate and legible.\n- The existing `--json` callers are unaffected, because neither passes `--quiet`.\n- The guard is one more branch, and it must sit ahead of the quiet branch in the dispatch.\n\n**Alternatives Rejected**:\n- Last flag wins: order-dependent behavior that is invisible in the command line a caller writes.\n- Quiet wins over JSON: a caller that asked for an object would get a string, and its parser would fail somewhere else with no clue why.\n- JSON wins over quiet: the flag would appear to be accepted while doing nothing, which is worse than an error.\n\n---\n","_meta":{"cognition.ai/linesAdded":1,"cognition.ai/linesRemoved":1}}],"locations":[{"path":"/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.worktrees/223-deepseek-final/specs/zz-bench-authoring/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag/plan.md"}],"rawInput":{"file_path":"/Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Code_Environment/Public/.worktrees/223-deepseek-final/specs/zz-bench-authoring/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag/plan.md"},"_meta":{"cognition.ai/inferenceToolName":"edit"}}

A shell caller that needs only the recommendation must either grep for `Recommended Level:` or invoke `--json` and parse the object with a JSON tool. Both approaches are heavier than the task and couple the caller to the report layout.\n\nThere is no compact text mode. Adding one by changing the default report would break every human reader and any caller that compares output, so the capability has to be opt-in.\n\n### Purpose\n\nProvide a stable, one-line text result through `--quiet` so scripts and workflow prompts can capture the recommendation directly, while every existing invocation keeps its current output.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n\n- Accept a boolean `--quiet` option in the existing argument loop, in any position relative to the other options.\n- In text mode, write exactly one stdout line in the default report's format, for example `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)`.\n- Document the flag in the file-header OPTIONS block and in `show_help` output.\n- Preserve the current default text report, `--json` object, scoring, confidence, phase calculation, exit codes, and stderr messages.\n- Add a focused regression test that exercises quiet text, default text, JSON, JSON plus quiet, and the error path.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Changing scoring thresholds, level names, confidence, or phase recommendation logic.\n- Adding a short `-q` alias, a `--verbose` counterpart, or any new output format such as key=value or level-only numeric output.\n- Refactoring `output_text`, `output_json`, or the argument parser beyond the new branch.\n- Editing callers or workflow reference documents outside the script's own header and help text.\n\n### Files to Change\n\n| File Path | Change Type | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Modify | Add `--quiet`, document it, and emit the single-line text result. |\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/recommend-level-quiet.vitest.ts` | Create | Regression coverage for quiet, default, JSON, and error behavior. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-001 | The argument parser must accept `--quiet` as a boolean flag regardless of option order, and must continue to reject unknown options with the existing message and exit code 1. |\n| REQ-002 | In text mode with `--quiet`, stdout must contain exactly one line matching `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)` followed by a newline, with no leading blank line and no score, breakdown, or phase sections. |\n| REQ-003 | Without `--quiet`, the default text report and the `--json` object for a given input must remain byte-identical to their pre-change output. |\n| REQ-004 | `--quiet` must not change the computed level, total score, confidence, phase fields, exit status, or stderr text for any input; validation errors must still go to stderr only. |\n\n### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-005 | The file-header OPTIONS block and `show_help` must document `--quiet`; `--quiet --help` must still print help and exit 0. |\n| REQ-006 | When `--quiet` and `--json` are both supplied, the unchanged JSON object must be emitted and no text line must appear. |\n| REQ-007 | A focused regression test must cover quiet single-line output, unchanged default text output, JSON with and without quiet, help precedence, and an error path. |\n\n> Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,\n> which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- **SC-001**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 50 --files 2 --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)` and exits 0.\n- **SC-002**: The same invocation without `--quiet` produces output byte-identical to the captured pre-change baseline, including the leading and trailing blank lines.\n- **SC-003**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 500 --files 15 --auth --api --db --architectural --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 3 (Full)`.\n- **SC-004**: The focused test passes and `validate.sh` reports `RESULT: PASSED` for this packet.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:risks -->\n## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |\n|------|------|--------|------------|\n| Dependency | Bash 3.2 compatibility on macOS | New syntax could break the script on the default shell | Use the existing `[[ ]]` and `case` patterns; run `bash -n` and the real script under `/bin/bash`. |\n| Risk | Quiet output inherits the leading blank line from `output_text` | A consumer capturing the output gets an empty first line | Use a dedicated output function and assert the exact line count and content. |\n| Risk | A refactor of the dispatch changes default output | Existing callers and snapshots break | Capture baselines before editing and diff every default path after. |\n| Risk | The `--json` and `--quiet` combination is ambiguous | Two consumers expect different output | ADR-001 fixes JSON precedence and the test covers it. |\n| Risk | The quiet line drifts from the default recommendation line | Two formats for one value | Assert the quiet line equals the default report's recommendation line in the test. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->\n\n---\n\n## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n\n- **NFR-P01**: The change adds one boolean check to the output dispatch and must not introduce measurable runtime cost or new subprocesses.\n- **NFR-P02**: Quiet output must be newline-terminated and safe to capture with `$(...)` without stripping meaningful content.\n\n### Security\n\n- **NFR-S01**: The flag adds no new input parsing beyond a boolean and introduces no secrets, environment reads, file writes, or network access.\n- **NFR-S02**: Existing validation errors must remain on stderr so quiet stdout stays machine-safe.\n\n### Reliability\n\n- **NFR-R01**: Exit codes must remain `0` for success and `1` for user error, matching the script's documented taxonomy.\n- **NFR-R02**: Output selection must be deterministic and exclusive: JSON first, then quiet text, then the default text report.\n\n---\n\n## 8. EDGE CASES\n\n### Data Boundaries\n\n- Empty or missing `--loc`/`--files`: the existing error path applies unchanged, with or without `--quiet`.\n- Zero values for both inputs: the existing error path applies unchanged.\n- Very large values: scoring is unchanged; quiet prints the same level the default report would print.\n- Repeated `--quiet`: the flag is idempotent and sets the same boolean.\n\n### Error Scenarios\n\n- `--quiet` with no `--loc` or `--files`: stderr message and exit 1 unchanged; stdout stays empty.\n- `--quiet` with a non-numeric value: the existing numeric validation error and exit 1 apply.\n- `--quiet=true`: not a supported form; the unknown-option error applies.\n- `--quiet --json`: JSON output wins, per ADR-001 in `plan.md`.\n- `--quiet --help`: help wins because `show_help` exits during parsing; exit 0.\n- `--no-recommend-phases --quiet`: quiet output is identical, since the phase section is suppressed in quiet mode either way.\n\n---\n\n## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT\n\n| Dimension | Score | Triggers |\n|-----------|-------|----------|\n| Scope | 8/25 | One shell script, one test file, no systems or data. |\n| Risk | 5/25 | Output-regression risk only; no auth, API, DB, or schema. |\n| Research | 3/20 | Parser and output paths are local and already mapped. |\n| Multi-Agent | 0/15 | Single owner; no parallel workstreams. |\n| Coordination | 4/15 | Script, test, and help text move together. |\n| **Total** | **20/100** | **Level 3 packet; implementation complexity is Level 0-1.** |\n\nThe score measures implementation complexity, not documentation depth. The packet carries Level 3 because the authoring contract requires the full planning set; the code change itself is small and isolated.\n\n---\n\n## 10. RISK MATRIX\n\n| Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|\n| R-001 | Default text or JSON output changes unintentionally. | High | Low | Capture baselines before editing and diff both paths after. |\n| R-002 | Quiet output includes a blank line or extra section. | Medium | Medium | Dedicated function plus exact one-line assertion. |\n| R-003 | `--json` plus `--quiet` produces mixed output. | Low | Medium | JSON precedence recorded in ADR-001 and tested. |\n| R-004 | New option parsing breaks an existing flag. | Low | Low | Keep the parser change to one case arm and rerun the flag matrix. |\n\n---\n\n## 11. ARCHITECTURE\n\n### Pattern\n\nSingle-file bash CLI with a linear pipeline: parse arguments into globals, calculate scores, determine the level, then dispatch to one output formatter.\n\n### Key Components\n\n- **Argument parser**: the `while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]` loop in section 5 of the script; owns flag acceptance and validation.\n- **Scoring functions**: `calculate_loc_score`, `calculate_files_score`, `calculate_risk_score`, `calculate_complexity_score`, and `determine_level`; unchanged.\n- **Output dispatch**: the final `if` in section 7 that selects JSON or text; gains the quiet branch.\n- **`output_quiet`**: new function in section 4 that prints the single recommended-level line.\n- **`output_text` and `output_json`**: existing formatters; unchanged.\n\n### Data Flow\n\n`argv` → parser sets `LOC`, `FILES`, risk flags, `JSON_OUTPUT`, and the new `QUIET` → scoring functions fill `TOTAL_SCORE` → `determine_level` sets `RECOMMENDED_LEVEL` and `LEVEL_NAME` → `calculate_confidence` and `determine_phasing` run as today → dispatch chooses `output_json`, `output_quiet`, or `output_text`.\n\nThe dispatch is exclusive and ordered: JSON first, quiet text second, default text last. Quiet mode never modifies scores or reaches the JSON path.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:architecture -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:affected-surfaces -->\n## FIX ADDENDUM: AFFECTED SURFACES\n\n| Surface | Current Role | Action | Verification |\n|---------|--------------|--------|--------------|\n| `recommend-level.sh` argument parser | Accepts options and sets globals | Update | `bash -n`; `--quiet` accepted in any order; `--quiet=true` rejected |\n| `recommend-level.sh` output dispatch | Chooses JSON versus text | Update | JSON plus quiet stays JSON; quiet text is one line |\n| `output_text` | Human-readable report | Unchanged | Baseline diff is empty |\n| `output_json` | Machine-readable report | Unchanged | Baseline diff is empty and JSON parses |\n| `show_help` and file-header OPTIONS | Document the CLI surface | Update | Help lists `--quiet`; `--quiet --help` exits 0 |\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/intake-contract.md` | Documents `level_recommendation` as script output | Unchanged | Reference inspection found no line-by-line stdout parser |\n| `runtime/cli/tests/test-phase-system.js` | Invokes the script with `--json` | Unchanged | Existing test remains green |\n\nRequired inventories:\n- Same-class producers: `rg -n 'JSON_OUTPUT|output_text|output_json|Recommended Level:' .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh`.\n- Consumers of the changed surface: `rg -n 'recommend-level\\.sh' .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit --glob '!node_modules'`.\n- Matrix axes: flag state (absent, `--quiet`) crossed with output mode (text, JSON, help, error). A caller could pass both, and the script must choose one shape. Printing a text line alongside JSON would break every JSON consumer, while ignoring quiet in JSON mode keeps the machine contract intact.\n\n**Decision**: When `JSON_OUTPUT` is true, emit the unchanged JSON object and ignore `--quiet`. It always prints a multi-section human report unless `--json` is supplied, so a caller that wants only the level must grep the report or parse JSON.\n\nThis packet specifies a minimal, opt-in `--quiet` flag. With the flag the script prints one line, `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`, and nothing else on stdout; without the flag every existing output path stays byte-identical.\n\n**Key Decisions**: Keep the flag long-form only; route quiet output through a dedicated function rather than modifying `output_text`; let `--json` take precedence when both flags are present.\n\n**Critical Dependencies**: None outside the script itself. The change uses the existing bash 3.2-compatible parser and output dispatch, with no new libraries, services, or data.\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## 1. PROBLEM & PURPOSE\n\n### Problem Statement\n\nThe script's text mode opens with a blank line, prints the recommendation, a score and confidence line, a per-factor breakdown, and a phase section. A shell caller that needs only the recommendation must either grep for `Recommended Level:` or invoke `--json` and parse the object with a JSON tool. Both approaches are heavier than the task and couple the caller to the report layout.\n\nThere is no compact text mode. Adding one by changing the default report would break every human reader and any caller that compares output, so the capability has to be opt-in.\n\n### Purpose\n\nProvide a stable, one-line text result through `--quiet` so scripts and workflow prompts can capture the recommendation directly, while every existing invocation keeps its current output.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n\n- Accept a boolean `--quiet` option in the existing argument loop, in any position relative to the other options.\n- In text mode, write exactly one stdout line: `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`.\n- Document the flag in the file-header OPTIONS block and in `show_help` output.\n- Preserve the current default text report, `--json` object, scoring, confidence, phase calculation, exit codes, and stderr messages.\n- Add a focused regression test that exercises quiet text, default text, JSON, JSON plus quiet, and the error path.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Changing scoring thresholds, level names, confidence, or phase recommendation logic.\n- Adding a short `-q` alias, a `--verbose` counterpart, or any new output format such as key=value or level-only numeric output.\n- Refactoring `output_text`, `output_json`, or the argument parser beyond the new branch.\n- Editing callers or workflow reference documents outside the script's own header and help text.\n\n### Files to Change\n\n| File Path | Change Type | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Modify | Add `--quiet`, document it, and emit the single-line text result. |\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/recommend-level-quiet.vitest.ts` | Create | Regression coverage for quiet, default, JSON, and error behavior. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-001 | The argument parser must accept `--quiet` as a boolean flag regardless of option order, and must continue to reject unknown options with the existing message and exit code 1. |\n| REQ-002 | In text mode with `--quiet`, stdout must contain exactly one line matching `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)` followed by a newline, with no leading blank line and no score, breakdown, or phase sections. |\n| REQ-003 | Without `--quiet`, the default text report and the `--json` object for a given input must remain byte-identical to their pre-change output. |\n| REQ-004 | `--quiet` must not change the computed level, total score, confidence, phase fields, exit status, or stderr text for any input; validation errors must still go to stderr only. |\n\n### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-005 | The file-header OPTIONS block and `show_help` must document `--quiet`; `--quiet --help` must still print help and exit 0. |\n| REQ-006 | When `--quiet` and `--json` are both supplied, the unchanged JSON object must be emitted and no text line must appear. |\n| REQ-007 | A focused regression test must cover quiet single-line output, unchanged default text output, JSON with and without quiet, help precedence, and an error path. |\n\n> Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,\n> which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n\n- **NFR-P01**: The change adds one boolean check to the output dispatch and must not introduce measurable runtime cost or new subprocesses.\n- **NFR-P02**: Quiet output must be newline-terminated and safe to capture with `$(...)` without stripping meaningful content.\n\n### Security\n\n- **NFR-S01**: The flag adds no new input parsing beyond a boolean and introduces no secrets, environment reads, file writes, or network access.\n- **NFR-S02**: Existing validation errors must remain on stderr so quiet stdout stays machine-safe.\n\n### Reliability\n\n- **NFR-R01**: Exit codes must remain `0` for success and `1` for user error, matching the script's documented taxonomy.\n- **NFR-R02**: Output selection must be deterministic and exclusive: JSON first, then quiet text, then the default text report.\n\n---\n\n## 8. EDGE CASES\n\n### Data Boundaries\n\n- Empty or missing `--loc`/`--files`: the existing error path applies unchanged, with or without `--quiet`.\n- Zero values for both inputs: the existing error path applies unchanged.\n- Very large values: scoring is unchanged; quiet prints the same level the default report would print.\n- Repeated `--quiet`: the flag is idempotent and sets the same boolean.\n\n### Error Scenarios\n\n- `--quiet` with no `--loc` or `--files`: stderr message and exit 1 unchanged; stdout stays empty.\n- `--quiet` with a non-numeric value: the existing numeric validation error and exit 1 apply.\n- `--quiet=true`: not a supported form; the unknown-option error applies.\n- `--quiet --json`: JSON output wins, per ADR-001 in `plan.md`.\n- `--quiet --help`: help wins because `show_help` exits during parsing; exit 0.\n- `--no-recommend-phases --quiet`: quiet output is identical, since the phase section is suppressed in quiet mode either way.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Add an opt-in --quiet flag that prints exactly the recommended-level line while leaving default text output, JSON output, scoring, and exit codes unchanged.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"recommend level quiet flag\"\n  - \"recommend-level --quiet\"\n  - \"quiet level recommendation\"\n  - \"add a quiet flag to recommend level sh\"\nimportance_tier: \"normal\"\ncontextType: \"general\"\n---\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core + level2-verify + level3-arch | v2.2 -->\n# Feature Specification: Add a quiet flag to recommend-level.sh\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->\n\n---\n\n## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY\n\n`recommend-level.sh` is the spec-kit helper that turns LOC, file count, and risk flags into a documentation-level recommendation. It always prints a multi-section human report unless `--json` is supplied, so a caller that wants only the level must grep the report or parse JSON.\n\nThis packet specifies a minimal, opt-in `--quiet` flag. With the flag the script prints one line, `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)` for a Level 0 result, and nothing else on stdout; without the flag every existing output path stays byte-identical.\n\n**Key Decisions**: Keep the flag long-form only; route quiet output through a dedicated function rather than modifying `output_text`; let `--json` take precedence when both flags are present.\n\n**Critical Dependencies**: None outside the script itself. The change uses the existing bash 3.2-compatible parser and output dispatch, with no new libraries, services, or data.\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## 1. METADATA\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| **Level** | 3 |\n| **Priority** | P2 |\n| **Status** | Draft |\n| **Created** | 2026-10-25 |\n| **Branch** | `scaffold/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag` |\n| **Component** | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->\n## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE\n\n### Problem Statement\n\nThe script's text mode opens with a blank line, prints the recommendation, a score and confidence line, a per-factor breakdown, and a phase section. A shell caller that needs only the recommendation must either grep for `Recommended Level:` or invoke `--json` and parse the object with a JSON tool. Both approaches are heavier than the task and couple the caller to the report layout.\n\nThere is no compact text mode. Adding one by changing the default report would break every human reader and any caller that compares output, so the capability has to be opt-in.\n\n### Purpose\n\nProvide a stable, one-line text result through `--quiet` so scripts and workflow prompts can capture the recommendation directly, while every existing invocation keeps its current output.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n\n- Accept a boolean `--quiet` option in the existing argument loop, in any position relative to the other options.\n- In text mode, write exactly one stdout line: `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`.\n- Document the flag in the file-header OPTIONS block and in `show_help` output.\n- Preserve the current default text report, `--json` object, scoring, confidence, phase calculation, exit codes, and stderr messages.\n- Add a focused regression test that exercises quiet text, default text, JSON, JSON plus quiet, and the error path.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Changing scoring thresholds, level names, confidence, or phase recommendation logic.\n- Adding a short `-q` alias, a `--verbose` counterpart, or any new output format such as key=value or level-only numeric output.\n- Refactoring `output_text`, `output_json`, or the argument parser beyond the new branch.\n- Editing callers or workflow reference documents outside the script's own header and help text.\n\n### Files to Change\n\n| File Path | Change Type | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Modify | Add `--quiet`, document it, and emit the single-line text result. |\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/recommend-level-quiet.vitest.ts` | Create | Regression coverage for quiet, default, JSON, and error behavior. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-001 | The argument parser must accept `--quiet` as a boolean flag regardless of option order, and must continue to reject unknown options with the existing message and exit code 1. |\n| REQ-002 | In text mode with `--quiet`, stdout must contain exactly one line matching `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)` followed by a newline, with no leading blank line and no score, breakdown, or phase sections. |\n| REQ-003 | Without `--quiet`, the default text report and the `--json` object for a given input must remain byte-identical to their pre-change output. |\n| REQ-004 | `--quiet` must not change the computed level, total score, confidence, phase fields, exit status, or stderr text for any input; validation errors must still go to stderr only. |\n\n### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-005 | The file-header OPTIONS block and `show_help` must document `--quiet`; `--quiet --help` must still print help and exit 0. |\n| REQ-006 | When `--quiet` and `--json` are both supplied, the unchanged JSON object must be emitted and no text line must appear. |\n| REQ-007 | A focused regression test must cover quiet single-line output, unchanged default text output, JSON with and without quiet, help precedence, and an error path. |\n\n> Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,\n> which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- **SC-001**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 50 --files 2 --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)` and exits 0.\n- **SC-002**: The same invocation without `--quiet` produces output byte-identical to the captured pre-change baseline, including the leading and trailing blank lines.\n- **SC-003**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 500 --files 15 --auth --api --db --architectural --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 3 (Full)`.\n- **SC-004**: The focused test passes and `validate.sh` reports `RESULT: PASSED` for this packet.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:risks -->\n## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |\n|------|------|--------|------------|\n| Dependency | Bash 3.2 compatibility on macOS | New syntax could break the script on the default shell | Use the existing `[[ ]]` and `case` patterns; run `bash -n` and the real script under `/bin/bash`. |\n| Risk | Quiet output inherits the leading blank line from `output_text` | A consumer capturing the output gets an empty first line | Use a dedicated output function and assert the exact line count and content. |\n| Risk | A refactor of the dispatch changes default output | Existing callers and snapshots break | Capture baselines before editing and diff every default path after. |\n| Risk | The `--json` and `--quiet` combination is ambiguous | Two consumers expect different output | ADR-001 fixes JSON precedence and the test covers it. |\n| Risk | The quiet line drifts from the default recommendation line | Two formats for one value | Assert the quiet line equals the default report's recommendation line in the test. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->\n\n---\n\n## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n\n- **NFR-P01**: The change adds one boolean check to the output dispatch and must not introduce measurable runtime cost or new subprocesses.\n- **NFR-P02**: Quiet output must be newline-terminated and safe to capture with `$(...)` without stripping meaningful content.\n\n### Security\n\n- **NFR-S01**: The flag adds no new input parsing beyond a boolean and introduces no secrets, environment reads, file writes, or network access.\n- **NFR-S02**: Existing validation errors must remain on stderr so quiet stdout stays machine-safe.\n\n### Reliability\n\n- **NFR-R01**: Exit codes must remain `0` for success and `1` for user error, matching the script's documented taxonomy.\n- **NFR-R02**: Output selection must be deterministic and exclusive: JSON first, then quiet text, then the default text report.\n\n---\n\n## 8. EDGE CASES\n\n### Data Boundaries\n\n- Empty or missing `--loc`/`--files`: the existing error path applies unchanged, with or without `--quiet`.\n- Zero values for both inputs: the existing error path applies unchanged.\n- Very large values: scoring is unchanged; quiet prints the same level the default report would print.\n- Repeated `--quiet`: the flag is idempotent and sets the same boolean.\n\n### Error Scenarios\n\n- `--quiet` with no `--loc` or `--files`: stderr message and exit 1 unchanged; stdout stays empty.\n- `--quiet` with a non-numeric value: the existing numeric validation error and exit 1 apply.\n- `--quiet=true`: not a supported form; the unknown-option error applies.\n- `--quiet --json`: JSON output wins, per ADR-001 in `plan.md`.\n- `--quiet --help`: help wins because `show_help` exits during parsing; exit 0.\n- `--no-recommend-phases --quiet`: quiet output is identical, since the phase section is suppressed in quiet mode either way.\n\n---\n\n## 9. COMPLEXITY ASSESSMENT\n\n| Dimension | Score | Triggers |\n|-----------|-------|----------|\n| Scope | 8/25 | One shell script, one test file, no systems or data. |\n| Risk | 5/25 | Output-regression risk only; no auth, API, DB, or schema. |\n| Research | 3/20 | Parser and output paths are local and already mapped. |\n| Multi-Agent | 0/15 | Single owner; no parallel workstreams. |\n| Coordination | 4/15 | Script, test, and help text move together. |\n| **Total** | **20/100** | **Level 3 packet; implementation complexity is Level 0-1.** |\n\nThe score measures implementation complexity, not documentation depth. The packet carries Level 3 because the authoring contract requires the full planning set; the code change itself is small and isolated.\n\n---\n\n## 10. RISK MATRIX\n\n| Risk ID | Description | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |\n|---------|-------------|--------|------------|------------|\n| R-001 | Default text or JSON output changes unintentionally. | High | Low | Capture baselines before editing and diff both paths after. |\n| R-002 | Quiet output includes a blank line or extra section. | Medium | Medium | Dedicated function plus exact one-line assertion. |\n| R-003 | `--json` plus `--quiet` produces mixed output. | Low | Medium | JSON precedence recorded in ADR-001 and tested. |\n| R-004 | New option parsing breaks an existing flag. | Low | Low | Keep the parser change to one case arm and rerun the flag matrix. |\n\n---\n\n## 11. Add an opt-in --quiet flag that prints exactly the recommended-level line while leaving default text output, JSON output, scoring, and exit codes unchanged.\"\ntrigger_phrases:\n  - \"recommend level quiet flag\"\n  - \"recommend-level --quiet\"\n  - \"quiet level recommendation\"\n  - \"add a quiet flag to recommend level sh\"\nimportance_tier: \"normal\"\ncontextType: \"general\"\n---\n<!-- SPECKIT_TEMPLATE_SOURCE: spec-core + level2-verify + level3-arch | v2.2 -->\n# Feature Specification: Add a quiet flag to recommend-level.sh\n\n<!-- SPECKIT_LEVEL: 3 -->\n\n---\n\n## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY\n\n`recommend-level.sh` is the spec-kit helper that turns LOC, file count, and risk flags into a documentation-level recommendation. It always prints a multi-section human report unless `--json` is supplied, so a caller that wants only the level must grep the report or parse JSON.\n\nThis packet specifies a minimal, opt-in `--quiet` flag. With the flag the script prints one line, `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`, and nothing else on stdout; without the flag every existing output path stays byte-identical.\n\n**Key Decisions**: Keep the flag long-form only; route quiet output through a dedicated function rather than modifying `output_text`; let `--json` take precedence when both flags are present.\n\n**Critical Dependencies**: None outside the script itself. The change uses the existing bash 3.2-compatible parser and output dispatch, with no new libraries, services, or data.\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:metadata -->\n## 1. METADATA\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| **Level** | 3 |\n| **Priority** | P2 |\n| **Status** | Draft |\n| **Created** | 2026-10-25 |\n| **Branch** | `scaffold/001-recommend-level-quiet-flag` |\n| **Component** | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:metadata -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:problem -->\n## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE\n\n### Problem Statement\n\nThe script's text mode opens with a blank line, prints the recommendation, a score and confidence line, a per-factor breakdown, and a phase section. A shell caller that needs only the recommendation must either grep for `Recommended Level:` or invoke `--json` and parse the object with a JSON tool. Both approaches are heavier than the task and couple the caller to the report layout.\n\nThere is no compact text mode. Adding one by changing the default report would break every human reader and any caller that compares output, so the capability has to be opt-in.\n\n### Purpose\n\nProvide a stable, one-line text result through `--quiet` so scripts and workflow prompts can capture the recommendation directly, while every existing invocation keeps its current output.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:scope -->\n## 3. SCOPE\n\n### In Scope\n\n- Accept a boolean `--quiet` option in the existing argument loop, in any position relative to the other options.\n- In text mode, write exactly one stdout line: `Recommended Level: <N> (<Name>)`.\n- Document the flag in the file-header OPTIONS block and in `show_help` output.\n- Preserve the current default text report, `--json` object, scoring, confidence, phase calculation, exit codes, and stderr messages.\n- Add a focused regression test that exercises quiet text, default text, JSON, JSON plus quiet, and the error path.\n\n### Out of Scope\n\n- Changing scoring thresholds, level names, confidence, or phase recommendation logic.\n- Adding a short `-q` alias, a `--verbose` counterpart, or any new output format such as key=value or level-only numeric output.\n- Refactoring `output_text`, `output_json`, or the argument parser beyond the new branch.\n- Editing callers or workflow reference documents outside the script's own header and help text.\n\n### Files to Change\n\n| File Path | Change Type | Description |\n|-----------|-------------|-------------|\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/spec/recommend-level.sh` | Modify | Add `--quiet`, document it, and emit the single-line text result. |\n| `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/recommend-level-quiet.vitest.ts` | Create | Regression coverage for quiet, default, JSON, and error behavior. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:requirements -->\n## 4. REQUIREMENTS\n\n### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-001 | The argument parser must accept `--quiet` as a boolean flag regardless of option order, and must continue to reject unknown options with the existing message and exit code 1. |\n| REQ-002 | In text mode with `--quiet`, stdout must contain exactly one line in the default report's format, for example `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)`, followed by a newline, with no leading blank line and no score, breakdown, or phase sections. |\n| REQ-003 | Without `--quiet`, the default text report and the `--json` object for a given input must remain byte-identical to their pre-change output. |\n| REQ-004 | `--quiet` must not change the computed level, total score, confidence, phase fields, exit status, or stderr text for any input; validation errors must still go to stderr only. |\n\n### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)\n\n| ID | Requirement |\n|----|-------------|\n| REQ-005 | The file-header OPTIONS block and `show_help` must document `--quiet`; `--quiet --help` must still print help and exit 0. |\n| REQ-006 | When `--quiet` and `--json` are both supplied, the unchanged JSON object must be emitted and no text line must appear. |\n| REQ-007 | A focused regression test must cover quiet single-line output, unchanged default text output, JSON with and without quiet, help precedence, and an error path. |\n\n> Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,\n> which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA\n\n- **SC-001**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 50 --files 2 --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 0 (Quick)` and exits 0.\n- **SC-002**: The same invocation without `--quiet` produces output byte-identical to the captured pre-change baseline, including the leading and trailing blank lines.\n- **SC-003**: `recommend-level.sh --loc 500 --files 15 --auth --api --db --architectural --quiet` prints exactly `Recommended Level: 3 (Full)`.\n- **SC-004**: The focused test passes and `validate.sh` reports `RESULT: PASSED` for this packet.\n<!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->\n\n---\n\n<!-- ANCHOR:risks -->\n## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES\n\n| Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |\n|------|------|--------|------------|\n| Dependency | Bash 3.2 compatibility on macOS | New syntax could break the script on the default shell | Use the existing `[[ ]]` and `case` patterns; run `bash -n` and the real script under `/bin/bash`. |\n| Risk | Quiet output inherits the leading blank line from `output_text` | A consumer capturing the output gets an empty first line | Use a dedicated output function and assert the exact line count and content. |\n| Risk | A refactor of the dispatch changes default output | Existing callers and snapshots break | Capture baselines before editing and diff every default path after. |\n| Risk | The `--json` and `--quiet` combination is ambiguous | Two consumers expect different output | ADR-001 fixes JSON precedence and the test covers it. |\n| Risk | The quiet line drifts from the default recommendation line | Two formats for one value | Assert the quiet line equals the default report's recommendation line in the test. |\n<!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->\n\n---\n\n## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS\n\n### Performance\n\n- **NFR-P01**: The change adds one boolean check to the output dispatch and must not introduce measurable runtime cost or new subprocesses.\n- **NFR-P02**: Quiet output must be newline-terminated and safe to capture with `$(...)` without stripping meaningful content.\n\n### Security\n\n- **NFR-S01**: The flag adds no new input parsing beyond a boolean and introduces no secrets, environment reads, file writes, or network access.\n- **NFR-S02**: Existing validation errors must remain on stderr so quiet stdout stays machine-safe.\n\n### Reliability\n\n- **NFR-R01**: Exit codes must remain `0` for success and `1` for user error, matching the script's documented taxonomy.\n- **NFR-R02**: Output selection must be deterministic and exclusive: JSON first, then quiet text, then the default text report.\n\n---\n\n## 8. EDGE CASES\n\n### Data Boundaries\n\n- Empty or missing `--loc`/`--files`: the existing error path applies unchanged, with or without `--quiet`.\n- Zero values for both inputs: the existing error path applies unchanged.\n- Very large values: scoring is unchanged; quiet prints the same level the default report would print.\n- Repeated `--quiet`: the flag is idempotent and sets the same boolean.\n\n### Error Scenarios\n\n- `--quiet` with no `--loc` or `--files`: stderr message and exit 1 unchanged; stdout stays empty.\n- `--quiet` with a non-numeric value: the existing numeric validation error and exit 1 apply.\n- `--quiet=true`: not a supported form; the unknown-option error applies.\n- `--quiet --json`: JSON output wins, per ADR-001 in `plan.md`.\n- `--quiet --help`: help wins because `show_help` exits during parsing; exit 0.\n- `--no-recommend-phases --quiet`: quiet output is identical, since the phase section is suppressed in quiet mode either way.\n\n---\n\n## 9. OVERVIEW\n\n### What Is This Reference?\n\nThis document provides comprehensive documentation for every validation rule enforced by the SpecKit system. It covers rule behavior, severity levels, detection patterns, and remediation steps for each validation check.\n\n**Core Purpose**:\n- **Rule Documentation** - Complete specifications for all validation checks\n- **Fix Instructions** - Clear remediation steps when validation fails\n- **Configuration Guide** - Environment variables and usage patterns\n\n### Core Principle\n\n> Validation ensures spec folders meet quality standards before claiming completion—preventing incomplete documentation from passing the Completion Verification Rule.\n\n### Severity Levels\n\n| Severity | Exit Code | Strict Mode | Description                       |\n| -------- | --------- | ----------- | --------------------------------- |\n| ERROR    | 2         | 2           | Validation failed, must fix       |\n| WARNING  | 0         | 0           | Passed with issues, should fix    |\n| INFO     | 0         | 0           | Informational, no action required |\n\nCLI taxonomy: `0` = success, `1` = user error, `2` = validation error, and `3` = system error. `--strict` selects the rules that only run under strict; a warning stays advice in both modes and never changes the exit code. A rule that should block reports an error itself.\n\n---\n\n## 2. RULE SUMMARY\n\n| Rule ID              | Severity | Applies To    | Description                                    |\n| -------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |\n| `FILE_EXISTS`        | ERROR    | All levels    | Required files present for documentation level |\n| `PLACEHOLDER_FILLED` | ERROR    | Core files    | No unfilled template placeholders              |\n| `LEVEL_DECLARED`     | INFO     | spec.md       | Level explicitly stated in metadata            |\n| `AC_COVERAGE`        | INFO     | acceptance-criteria.md | Advisory traceability scan over each criterion's Verification cell (on by default; `SPECKIT_AC_COVERAGE_ENFORCE=true` makes an under-floor result fail) |\n| `AC_CLOSURE`         | ERROR    | acceptance-criteria.md | Closure gate for Levels 2/3/3+: unmet criteria block a completion claim, waivers must cite a real ADR |\n| `CONTINUITY_FRESHNESS` | WARNING | completion claims | Opt-in strict-only completion freshness check |\n| `ANCHORS_VALID`      | ERROR    | spec docs with anchored templates | Anchors present, paired and not nested (adr-NNN may hold adr-NNN-*) |\n| `FOLDER_NAMING`      | ERROR    | Folder path   | Folder follows ###-short-name convention       |\n| `FRONTMATTER_VALID`  | ERROR    | spec docs     | YAML frontmatter properly structured           |\n| `COMPLEXITY_MATCH`   | WARNING  | All levels    | Content metrics match declared level           |\n| `AI_PROTOCOLS`       | ERROR    | Level 3/3+    | AI execution protocols present                 |\n| `LEVEL_MATCH`        | ERROR    | All files     | Level consistent across all spec files         |\n| `SPEC_DOC_SUFFICIENCY` | ERROR  | spec docs, goal.md | Anchor sufficiency; for `goal.md` also the durable budget (one limit: fail past 4000) and binding-row existence |\n| `FRONTMATTER_VALUES` | WARNING  | packet docs   | `contextType` or `importance_tier` outside sk-create-frontmatter's `frontmatter-values.json`;
